transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. Ever since my car accident two weeks ago, I just can’t think straight or focus long enough to finish anything, even simple tasks at work. It's gotten to the point where I'm really falling behind and my manager is starting to notice.
Have you experienced any memory problems or difficulty learning new information since the accident?

I haven't really noticed any specific memory loss or trouble learning new things. It's more that my mind just goes totally blank when I'm trying to read something or make simple decisions. I'll just stare at a page or an email and can't focus enough to actually process it.
Do you also feel unusually tired or lacking in energy, which might be contributing to your difficulty in focusing?
I don't really feel unusually tired or like I'm lacking energy. Instead, it feels more like my mind just goes completely blank, or I get too overwhelmed to actually process what's in front of me.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of anxiety, sadness, or irritability since the car accident, or is it primarily the cognitive symptoms like blanking and overwhelm that you're struggling with?

It’s definitely not just the focus issues—I’ve been feeling extremely irritable and anxious lately. I find myself snapping at my sister over simple questions about car insurance and raising my voice at my coworkers before I even realize it. Plus, my heart starts racing whenever memories of the crash pop up, my chest gets tight when I think about driving, and I literally jump out of my skin at any sudden noises.

Can you tell me more about these memories of the crash - do you experience them as flashbacks, where you feel like you're reliving the accident, or are they more like intrusive thoughts or images that you can't stop thinking about?

They are definitely sudden pictures and sounds that just pop into my head, like the sound of the crash, the glass shattering, and the smell of burning rubber. It feels so real that my heart starts racing and I feel like I'm right back in the driver's seat again, and I just can't shut it off.
Have you been avoiding certain places, activities, or situations because they remind you of the car accident or trigger these intrusive memories and anxiety?

Yes, I've been going completely out of my way to avoid the intersection where the crash happened, and I make excuses to avoid driving or being in a car at night because my chest gets so tight and I feel like I'll lose it. It's gotten so bad that I've been bailing on family events and even struggling to get myself to drive to work.
When you experience these intrusive memories or flashbacks, do you feel like you're detached from yourself or the world around you, as if you're observing things from outside your body?

Yes, actually, I do. Sometimes everything suddenly feels weirdly far away and fake, like I’m watching a movie of my own life instead of being in my body. I just completely space out like that until it slowly wears off.

Can you tell me more about how often these feelings of detachment or spaciness happen, and are they usually triggered by something specific, like the memories of the crash, or do they occur unexpectedly?

They happen sometimes, especially when I'm riding in a car or even just walking down the street. It feels like everything suddenly gets fake and far away, like I'm watching a movie of my own life, and it takes a while for me to slowly snap out of it.
Have you experienced any of these symptoms, such as the intrusive memories, anxiety, or feelings of detachment, before the car accident, or are they entirely new since the accident occurred?

No, I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. All of these symptoms are completely new and only started right after the car accident two weeks ago. Before the crash, I was completely fine and didn't have any of these issues.
